summary.intent: Fix Google OAuth login in a Tauri desktop app that was failing with Error 400 invalid_request because Google rejects the tauri://localhost redirect URI scheme.
summary.outcome: Implemented a temporary localhost HTTP callback server in Rust to handle the OAuth redirect on http://localhost:{port}/callback, wired it into the TypeScript auth flow, fixed several follow-on bugs (Tauri event permissions, TCP body parsing, event scoping, nonce validation), and resolved all 6 Copilot PR review comments.

repo: Tauri v2 uses capability-based permissions in apps/desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json — event listener API requires core:event:default to be explicitly listed
Google OAuth client ID is 164556913424-uif44is1apnl7rqc9a2ac7vn8u9dq0ee; preferred pre-registerable callback ports are 14200, 14201, 14202
The rand crate version is 0.8, which uses thread_rng() — not the newer rand::rng() API
Project has a .planning/debug/ directory used by the gsd-debugger subagent system for session state tracking
Cargo.lock picks up unrelated version bumps (e.g. cipherbox-fuse) during dev builds; must be stashed/discarded before committing OAuth-only fixes

code.finding: Original single read() call could not capture POST body that arrived in a separate TCP segment from headers, causing JSON parse failure; fixed with Content-Length-aware body accumulation loop

OAuth callback server now uses an absolute Instant deadline (not per-connection timeout reset), port-scoped event names (oauth-callback-{port}), random nonce embedded in callback HTML and validated on POST, and POPUP_COUNTER.load() instead of hardcoded 0..99 range for popup cleanup
Added core:event:default permission; without it Tauri v2 blocks listen() calls from the webview with 'event.listen not allowed'
getGoogleCredential() now calls start_oauth_server Tauri command first, uses returned port and event_name for scoped event listener, replaces old localStorage-polling approach

workflow: Google OAuth rejects tauri:// scheme URIs entirely — any Tauri app doing OAuth needs a real http://localhost callback server
GITHUB_TOKEN env var injected at the shell level overrides gh auth login stored credentials; unset inside a subshell doesn't propagate — must use env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh ... as a prefix workaround

When writing a minimal HTTP server in Rust without hyper/axum, a single TcpStream read() is insufficient for POST requests — headers and body may arrive in separate TCP segments and require Content-Length-aware accumulation

friction: GITHUB_TOKEN env var was injected at a level the Bash tool cannot unset; required env -u GITHUB_TOKEN prefix on every gh command and blocked the gh pr create flow entirely until the user cleared it in their own terminal
Tauri v2 capability permission error (core:event:default missing) only surfaced at runtime after dev server restart, not at compile time
Single TCP read() bug caused a 'Failed to parse callback data' regression that required a second debugging pass
Dev server had to be started 5+ times across the session due to app not appearing in taskbar, permission errors, and iterative Rust fixes requiring recompilation
git pull failed at session start due to divergent branches with no reconcile strategy configured
Cargo.lock accumulated an unrelated cipherbox-fuse version bump that had to be identified and discarded before committing
open_items: Redirect URIs http://localhost:14200/callback, http://localhost:14201/callback, http://localhost:14202/callback must be manually added to the Google Cloud Console OAuth client before production builds will work

Random port fallback was removed — if all three preferred ports (14200-14202) are busy, OAuth fails fast with an error rather than trying a random port; may need revisiting for constrained environments
core:event:default capability uses windows: ["*"] scope; Copilot flagged this as too broad but was left as-is since OAuth popups load external URLs and cannot access Tauri APIs regardless
